name: The composers
note: Fifty composition events, one for each work in data/corpus/works.json that had none, plus ten commentaries. Composition events now name their work outright with a `work` field rather than relying on the title matcher, which guessed.

events.title: The village story cycles begin to be told
events.evidence: None, and that is the point: no text survives, only the ethnographic and comparative evidence that such cycles are always there.
events.note: The game's first corpus entry is one that cannot be read. It is still an economy.

events.title: The Bhimbetka painters are already at work when the game opens
events.evidence: Some seven hundred painted shelters in the Vindhyan sandstone, in superimposed layers; the earliest are far older than this date and the tradition runs on into the historic period.
events.note: The oldest thing in the corpus does not begin during the campaign. It is inherited.

events.title: The Brihadaranyaka: Yajnavalkya argues and then walks away
events.evidence: The text itself within the Shatapatha Brahmana's recension, and the linguistic stratum of its Sanskrit.
events.note: It contains a woman, Gargi, asking the question nobody else in the room will ask.

events.title: The Chandogya: tat tvam asi, argued through eleven examples
events.evidence: The text as transmitted in the Samavedic shakhas, and its citation by later commentators.

events.title: The Katha Upanishad: a boy questions Death and is answered
events.evidence: The text's language, which is later than the prose Upanishads, and its verse form.

events.title: Yaska's Nirukta: the first etymological science
events.evidence: The text itself, which quotes and disputes earlier etymologists by name — so it is not the first attempt, only the first to survive.

events.title: Pingala's Chandahshastra: metre, and binary numbers on the way
events.evidence: The sutras themselves, whose enumeration of metrical patterns uses a positional binary scheme and the Fibonacci sequence.
events.note: Written to classify poetic metres. Contains binary arithmetic as a side effect.

events.title: The Bhagavad Gita is set into the Mahabharata
events.evidence: Its position within the Bhishma Parva, and the linguistic and doctrinal layers that mark it as an insertion.

events.title: The Jataka stories are collected around the verses
events.evidence: The Pali verses in the canon with their prose frames, and the same stories carved on the Bharhut and Sanchi railings.
events.note: Carved on a stupa railing before they were written down. Stone can be a manuscript.

events.title: The Dhammapada is fixed as a verse anthology
events.evidence: The Pali recension, the Gandhari version found in Khotan, and Chinese and Sanskrit parallels.

events.title: Nagarjuna's Mulamadhyamakakarika
events.evidence: The Sanskrit verses preserved in Chandrakirti's commentary, and Tibetan and Chinese translations.

events.title: Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakosha and its own commentary
events.evidence: The verses and bhasya, lost in Sanskrit for centuries and recovered from a Tibetan monastery in 1935.
events.note: Rahul Sankrityayan photographed the palm leaf in Tibet. The Sanskrit came home on film.

events.title: Dharmakirti's Pramanavarttika: logic pushed to its edge
events.evidence: The Sanskrit text and its Tibetan commentarial tradition, which is still taught.

events.title: Umaswati's Tattvartha Sutra, accepted by both Jain sects
events.evidence: The sutra text, which Digambara and Svetambara traditions both transmit with their own commentaries.
events.note: One text both halves of a schism agree on. There are not many.

events.title: The Jain Agamas are carried orally through famine and schism
events.evidence: The Svetambara canon as fixed at Valabhi, and the Digambara position that the original canon was already lost.

events.title: The Manusmriti is compiled
events.evidence: The text's metrical and doctrinal layers, and its citation by later dharmashastra commentators.
events.note: A prescriptive text, not a description of how anyone lived. The game should never confuse the two.

events.title: Bharata's Natyashastra: theatre, dance, music and rasa in one treatise
events.evidence: The surviving recensions and Abhinavagupta's tenth-century commentary, which preserves readings now lost.

events.title: The Charaka Samhita takes its surviving form
events.evidence: The text as redacted by Dridhabala, and the Bower manuscript's parallel passages.

events.title: The Sushruta Samhita: surgery, and a hundred and twenty-one instruments
events.evidence: The text with its later Nagarjuna redaction, and the Bower manuscript fragments.
events.note: Describes rhinoplasty using a forehead flap. The technique reached Europe in 1794 via a report from Pune.

events.title: Vatsyayana's Kamasutra sets out the sixty-four arts
events.evidence: The text and Yashodhara's thirteenth-century commentary.

events.title: The Krishi-Parashara: rainfall measured, oxen costed, seed treated
events.evidence: The text itself, which gives rain-gauge measurements by nakshatra and the cost of maintaining a plough team.
events.note: An agricultural manual that tells you what a pair of oxen costs to keep. The economy, written down.

events.title: Surapala's Vrikshayurveda: the science of trees
events.evidence: A single manuscript in the Bodleian, edited only in the twentieth century.

events.title: Bhoja's Samarangana Sutradhara: architecture, and machines
events.evidence: The text, with its chapters on town planning, temple form and yantra.

events.title: The Mayamata codifies the southern building canon
events.evidence: The text, and its correspondence with what the Chola temples actually do.

events.title: Sharngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara, written at Devagiri
events.evidence: The text, which both the Hindustani and Carnatic traditions treat as the last common authority.
events.note: Written just before the traditions parted. Both still cite it.

events.title: The Rasaratnakara and the alchemical turn in medicine
events.evidence: The surviving text, attributed to a Nagarjuna who is not the philosopher.

events.title: Mahavira's Ganita Sara Sangraha, written for the Rashtrakuta court
events.evidence: The text, which states that a number divided by zero remains unchanged — and is wrong, and says it plainly.
events.note: The first Indian text purely on mathematics, with no astronomy attached.

events.title: Nilakantha's Tantrasangraha
events.evidence: The text, dated by its own chronogram to 1501, with the series expansions of the Kerala school.

events.title: Jyesthadeva's Yuktibhasha: the proofs, in Malayalam
events.evidence: The text, which gives demonstrations rather than results — and is written in the spoken language, not Sanskrit.
events.note: Calculus results with proofs, in a regional language, a century before Newton.

events.title: The Sangam anthologies are assembled
events.evidence: The eight anthologies and ten songs themselves, with their colophons naming poets and patrons.

events.title: The Alvars compose the four thousand
events.evidence: The hymns, and the temple inscriptions that endow their recitation.

events.title: Shudraka's Mrichchhakatika: a play about a poor merchant and a courtesan
events.evidence: The text, whose prakrits and stagecraft place it early in the surviving drama.

events.title: Al-Biruni finishes the Tarikh al-Hind
events.evidence: The Arabic text, which states its own date and its method: learn the language, read the sources, report the disagreements.
events.note: He learned Sanskrit to write it, and said outright where he thought his own sources were unreliable.

events.title: Amir Khusrau writes in Persian and in Hindavi
events.evidence: The five divans, the Khamsa, and the Hindavi verses attributed to him.

events.title: Babur writes the Baburnama in Chagatai
events.evidence: The Chagatai text, with its gaps, its botany and its account of the author's own failures.
events.note: An emperor's memoir that records losing. It also catalogues the fruit.

events.title: The Padshahnama is compiled and illustrated
events.evidence: The manuscript and its paintings, and the succession of court historians named in it.

events.title: The Sharanas compose vachanas in spoken Kannada
events.evidence: The vachana corpus itself, signed with each author's ankita, and the trades its authors name as their own.
events.note: Written by washerwomen, cobblers, boatmen and ferrymen. Signed. In their own language.

events.title: Kabir's dohas circulate before anyone writes them down
events.evidence: Three separate written traditions — the Bijak, the Guru Granth Sahib and the Rajasthani manuscripts — which do not agree.
events.note: Three recensions that disagree is what an oral corpus looks like when it finally hits paper.

events.title: Tulsidas writes the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi
events.evidence: The text, which dates its own beginning, and the manuscript tradition from Varanasi.

events.title: The Adi Granth is compiled, and later sealed as the Guru
events.evidence: The Kartarpur manuscript, and the 1708 declaration that the book itself succeeds the human Gurus.
events.note: It includes Hindu and Muslim voices alongside the Gurus'. The canon is deliberately not one community's.

events.title: Tukaram's abhangas
events.evidence: The abhanga corpus and the Dehu manuscript tradition.

events.title: Gandhi writes Hind Swaraj on a ship
events.evidence: The Gujarati text, written in ten days aboard the Kildonan Castle, and its immediate proscription.

events.title: Tagore's Gitanjali, and then his own English of it
events.evidence: The Bengali collection and the 1912 English Song Offerings, which is a different book.

events.title: Bankim's Anandamath
events.evidence: The Bengali novel and its serialisation in Bangadarshan.

events.title: Ambedkar publishes Annihilation of Caste, the speech he was not allowed to give
events.evidence: The printed text, and the correspondence with the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal that cancelled the address.
events.note: Written to be spoken, refused a platform, and printed at the author's own expense. It outlasted the platform.

events.title: Nehru writes The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort
events.evidence: The manuscript, written in prison between April and September 1944.

events.title: The Constitution is drafted, debated and adopted
events.evidence: The Constituent Assembly Debates, twelve volumes of them, and the calligraphed original.
events.note: Three years of argument, recorded verbatim. The last entry in the corpus, and the only one the reader is inside.

events.title: The Vetala Panchavimshati: twenty-five riddles told by a corpse
events.evidence: The versions embedded in the Kathasaritsagara and the Brihatkathamanjari.

events.title: Narayana's Hitopadesha reworks the Panchatantra
events.evidence: The text, which names its source, and the manuscript tradition from Bengal.

events.title: The Sukasaptati: seventy tales told by a parrot to delay a wife
events.evidence: The Sanskrit recensions, and the Persian Tutinama that derives from them.

events.title: Shabara's commentary on the Mimamsa Sutras
events.evidence: The bhasya, which is the base text for every later Mimamsa argument about how a sentence means anything.

events.title: Shankara's commentaries on the Upanishads, the Gita and the Brahma Sutras
events.evidence: The bhasyas themselves, and the fact that later schools define themselves by disagreeing with them.
events.note: A commentary can be more read than what it comments on. This is how an endowment keeps paying.

events.title: Ramanuja's Sribhasya answers Shankara
events.evidence: The text, and the Srirangam temple's inscriptions recording its teaching.

events.title: Vachaspati Mishra writes on every school, including ones he does not hold
events.evidence: Commentaries surviving on Nyaya, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa and Vedanta, by one hand.
events.note: He explained his opponents' systems well enough that his opponents used his explanations.

events.title: Abhinavagupta's Abhinavabharati preserves a Natyashastra now lost
events.evidence: The commentary, which quotes readings and whole earlier commentators that survive nowhere else.
events.note: We read the Natyashastra partly through a man who was reading a better copy.

events.title: Mallinatha's commentaries fix how the kavya is read
events.evidence: The commentaries on Kalidasa, Bharavi, Magha and Sri Harsha, which every later edition follows.

events.title: Sayana's commentary on the whole Rigveda, at the Vijayanagara court
events.evidence: The bhasya, undertaken with state support, and the colophons naming the patron.
events.note: A state paying for a complete commentary on a three-thousand-year-old text. That is the knowledge economy at full stretch.

events.title: Bhaskara I writes the earliest surviving prose commentary on Aryabhata
events.evidence: The commentary, the earliest surviving Sanskrit prose on mathematics, dated by its own examples.

events.title: Hemachandra's Siddha-Hema: a grammar for six languages at once
events.evidence: The text, commissioned by Jayasimha Siddharaja and carried through Gujarat on an elephant.
events.note: A grammar given a public procession. Somebody thought language was worth a parade.

events.title: Jain commentators fix the Prakrit canon with Sanskrit glosses
events.evidence: The churni and tika layers on the Agamas, which record variant readings the base text had already lost.
